paragraphs: In theory, all people agree that they can make mistakes. But in real life, this idea does not change what they do. Everyone knows that he can be wrong. But few people try to protect themselves from their own mistakes. They feel very sure about some opinions. They do not think that these opinions can be wrong too. Kings with total power often feel this way about almost everything. Other people are in a better position. Sometimes others say that they are wrong, and sometimes they accept this. But they still feel totally sure about some opinions. These are the opinions of all the people around them. A man who does not trust his own ideas often trusts "the world" completely.

For each person, "the world" is only the part of it that he knows. It is his political party, his religious group, his church or his social class. If a man thinks of his whole country or his whole time, he is quite open-minded. He knows that other times, countries, churches and groups have thought the opposite. Many still think the opposite today. But this does not shake his trust. He lets his own world be right against all the other worlds. It never worries him that only chance chose his world. The same causes that made him a member of the English Church in London would make him a Buddhist or a follower of Confucius in Pekin. But it is very clear that a time in history can be wrong, like a person. Every time in the past had many opinions that later times saw as false and even stupid. In the same way, future times will reject many of our common opinions today.

Some people will answer this idea in the following way. Stopping wrong ideas is like any other act of the state. The state always acts on its own judgment. People have judgment so that they can use it. Is it right to tell them not to use it at all, because they can make mistakes? When they stop harmful ideas, they do not say that they are never wrong. They only do their duty and act on what they honestly believe. If we never acted on our opinions, nothing important would get done. An argument against all actions is not an argument against one action.

These people also say this. Governments and people must try to have the truest opinions. They must form them carefully. They must not force them on others if they are not sure. But when they are sure, it is not honest to do nothing. It is weak and afraid. Dangerous ideas can hurt people in this life or in another life. In the past, people attacked opinions that we now think are true. We must not make the same mistake, they say. But governments have made other mistakes too. They have made bad taxes and unfair wars. Should we stop all taxes and all wars because of this? People and governments must do their best. Nothing is totally certain, but we can be sure enough for daily life. We must think that our opinion is true when we decide what to do. So, they say, we can also stop bad men from spreading false and harmful ideas.
